text: You've created a role, granted it privileges, and watched the object browser change in real time. This lesson turns that hands-on experience into a set of habits worth carrying into every Snowflake account you work in.

Five habits, in order of how often you'll lean on them. Grant privileges to roles, and roles to users — never privileges directly to a person. Follow least privilege: grant only what a role needs today, and add more later rather than over-granting up front just to avoid a second request. Keep ACCOUNTADMIN membership to a tiny handful of people, and do day-to-day administration as SECURITYADMIN, USERADMIN, or SYSADMIN instead. Keep the separation of duties you saw in Lesson 4 — USERADMIN creates roles, SECURITYADMIN grants them — don't collapse that into ACCOUNTADMIN out of convenience. And audit regularly; grants made two years ago by someone who left the company don't fix themselves.

One habit worth a closer look: future grants. GRANT SELECT ON FUTURE TABLES IN SCHEMA applies automatically to tables that don't exist yet. Without it, every new table in a fast-moving schema needs its own manual grant — which means it will eventually get forgotten, either leaving a role locked out of something it needs, or leaving a table over-privileged because someone copy-pasted an old grant out of habit.

And SHOW GRANTS is how you check your work, in both directions. SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE tells you everything a given role can do. SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE tells you everything that currently has access to a specific object. Run both periodically — don't assume a grant made months ago still makes sense today.

Chapter 2 starts next: dynamic data masking. You now know how to control who gets into a table. Next, you'll learn how to control what they actually see once they're in — because having access and seeing raw values aren't the same thing.
